title: Sentiment-led Canary Ops and Statistical Contracts (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick experimental thinking doc for combining user sentiment signals with standard canary/A-B statistical contracts. This is intentionally informal — notes to shape a runbook and a small helper library for ops engineers and product managers.

Context and motivation:
- We run many LLM rollouts where qualitative user reaction (sentiment, safety flags, escalation messages) matters more than raw CTR or latency. Standard numeric SLOs miss subtle but critical signal shifts (tone, politeness, hallucination frequency).
- Need an ops pattern that: 1) mixes automated signal detectors (NLP sentiment, safety heuristics) with manual human checkpoints; 2) defines statistical gating for A/B tests that account for non-normal signal distributions and low base-rate events; 3) provides fast rollback and comms playbooks tuned for language-product failure modes.

High-level design:
1) Canary tiers: micro (0.1%-0.5%), small (1-5%), ramp (10-25%). Always pair micro canaries with synthetic traffic and instrumentation probes.
2) Signal buckets (prioritized): safety-critical (policy violations, toxicity), semantic correctness (hallucination rate proxies), user sentiment (positive/neutral/negative continuous score), latency/cost regressions, core functional metrics (task success).
3) Sentiment-lead gating: treat sentiment as a primary experiment metric for features that change phrasing/behavior. Use a two-stage test: (A) automated detector threshold breach > alert; (B) human review sample of n=200 sessions within 24h to classify severity and trend.

Sampling and allocation rules:
- Randomization: deterministic user hashing per route to maintain cohort continuity across rollouts.
- Exposure budgets: define a token/latency budget per cohort to prevent runaway cost spikes. If per-token spend in variant > 1.5x baseline for > 2 sequential hours, auto-decrease exposure.
- Fractional fallback: allocate traffic split at edge AB router so fallback to baseline can be instantaneous at <200ms failover.

Statistical contracts and tests (practical ops version):
- Primary test types: nonparametric Mann-Whitney U for continuous sentiment scores; bootstrap CI for medians; exact binomial for low-rate safety events.
- Minimum sample sizes: for sentiment median shift detection at delta=0.12 (effect size), target n=1,200 per arm (but allow staged analysis with alpha spending). For safety events with base rate 0.3%, require aggregated exposure such that expected count >= 10 before making decisions.
- Sequential testing: use alpha spending (Pocock-style) with predeclared interim checks at 24h and 72h. Document decision rule for each interim (stop for harm, continue, or increase sample).

Human-in-the-loop checkpoints:
- Trigger conditions: (a) automated sentiment drift > 2 standard deviations vs baseline for 3 consecutive windows (1h windows); (b) safety event rate >= threshold; (c) support tickets mentioning regression spike.
- Review band: on trigger, product + solutions engineer + SRE form quick review panel. Panel checklist: reproduce failure, check model variant fingerprint, review top 50 negative sessions, check tracing for latency/cost anomalies, look up canary synthetic probe results.
- Escalation tree: reviewer -> rollout lead -> oncall SRE -> director if incident meets P1 criteria. Keep communication templates ready.

Comms templates (short form ready to paste):
- Internal alert (ops channel): "[CANARY ALERT] route=/chat-lens variant=v3.11 exposure=2% signal=sentiment-drop -12% vs baseline. Trigger: automated detector. Action: pause ramp, review panel requested. Link: <link-to-dashboard>."
- Customer-facing: brief note scaffold to CS for sensitive regressions with suggested mitigation steps and ETA.

Synthetic traffic and probes:
- Maintain a small library (20-50 prompts) that exercise edge failure modes: ambiguous queries, multi-step instructions, hallucination-prone facts. Run these probes at every exposure change and store outputs to a artifact store for diffing.
- Expectation: if synthetic probe quality drops >10% (predefined proxy), prevent further exposure increase until reviewed.

Rollback and quick-fix mechanics:
- Fast rollback path: feature gate + model pin in the router. Rollback must complete a global fallback in <2 minutes for distributed routes and <30s for single-region slices.
- Partial rollback: ability to soften only tone/verbosity changes by swapping a normalization layer in the prompt pipeline.

Observability and dashboards (must have):
- Variant-comparative dashboard: median sentiment by minute, safety event counts, token cost ratio, p-value timeline for sequential tests.
- Session replay sampler: top negative sessions + anonymized text, model-decisions trace, latencies.
- Alerting: on-call channel + email + slack thread; tickets auto-created in JIRA when P1 or safety threshold crossed.

Checklist for a canary rollout (practical):
- Pre-rollout: define hypothesis, metrics, alpha spending plan, synthetic probe run, confirm observability panels, schedule review window, set exposure budget.
- Micro canary: run 24h with synthetic probes and daily review; collect at least 1,200 sentiment samples if possible.
- Ramp: enforce token/latency budget; run interim sequential tests at predeclared points.
- Post-roll: run regression evals vs curated prompt-set, store artifacts, retrospective and PR with learnings.

Known tradeoffs and open questions:
- Sentiment detectors are model-dependent and can drift; need to version detectors and calibrate with human labels periodically.
- Low base-rate safety signals remain hardest — will need specialized monitoring that prioritizes precision over recall and a separate escalation path.
- Cost vs sensitivity: tighter gating reduces user exposure to regressions but slows experiments. Define risk appetite per product area.

Next actions / TODOs:
- Prototype a small alpha spending helper in the rollout lib (Ben).
- Capture 300 labeled sessions to calibrate sentiment detector (Lina).
- Add synthetic probe health into the canary gating logic (SRE intern).
- Draft short handbook page for CS comms templates and postmortem checklist.

Notes and references:
- Relevant dashboards: CONFLUENCE:rr-monitoring/sentiment-dash (placeholder).
- Related work: ROAD-3124 (staged rollout contracts), PR repo/llm-rollout-pr#241.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally pragmatic — ops friendly rules + minimal statistical hygiene. Will iterate into a formal runbook once we validate signals on 3 rollouts.
